s1.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The patient is a 32-year-old woman
The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area
There are widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area
The patient has sparse and short eyebrow hairs
The patient has coarse and brittle scalp hairs
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia and widespread erythematous plaques

shortlist.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia and erythematous plaques with double-edged scale

shortlist.label: Erythroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of 90% of body surface area and progressive worsening of skin condition

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Sparse and short eyebrow hairs, and coarse and brittle scalp hairs

shortlist.label: Ichthyosis vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Coarse and brittle scalp hairs, and possible association with skin condition

raw.rationale: The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques and involvement of 90% of the body surface area, along with the specific findings from the skin biopsy and trichography, aligns closely with the clinical presentation of Pityriasis rubra pilaris.

rejected.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, the overall clinical presentation and specific trichography findings are more indicative of Pityriasis rubra pilaris than Psoriasis vulgaris.

rejected.label: Erythroderma
rejected.why: Erythroderma is a condition characterized by widespread redness and scaling, but the specific plaque morphology and hair findings in this patient are more characteristic of Pityriasis rubra pilaris.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Dermatomyositis typically presents with muscle weakness and specific skin manifestations such as Gottron's papules, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Ichthyosis vulgaris
rejected.why: Ichthyosis vulgaris is a genetic disorder characterized by dry, scaly skin, but it does not typically present with the acute onset and specific plaque morphology seen in this patient.
